top.line: RC2 of One Human, Nine Agents, Nineteen Hours: a 27-page draft, checked five ways, and a request for feedback.
top.para: The book of the talk built in a day now has a title and a second release candidate, published as a draft. It is written down the zoom from 3 to 10 to 30 pages, with 70 begun, and each chapter passes five checks. Its scenes are the controls at work: reviewers catching their own team, an objection kept, a hold before the talk. It ends with five steps to build your own, and asks for feedback on LinkedIn or as an issue on the book's repository.

in-short.line: A title, a 27-page draft, five checks per chapter, the controls as scenes, and a feedback request.
in-short.para: Feedback on LinkedIn, or as an issue on the book's repository.

so-far.line: From the talk on 29 October to RC1, the cast, the lab, and 301 commits on 2 November.
so-far.para: RC2 is the first edition ready to show anyone who wants to read it.

zoom.line: The same story at 3, 10, 30 and 70 pages, each drafted from the shorter one.
zoom.para: Five chapters: the creator's problem, the factory assembled, the factory runs, the stop, and the factory rebuilt and yours.

checks.line: Each chapter passes the storyteller, test-reader personas, the librarian, the researcher and security.
checks.para: On 3 November chapters 1 to 3 had passed; 4, 5 and the series page still needed security and the researcher, and some figures are still to come.

controls.line: The controls are the scenes: a reviewer's catch, an argument won, an objection kept, the hold.
controls.para: A reviewer in the same session is a second reading, not a second identity. Every scene is dramatised, says so, and names the records it rests on.

yours.line: Five steps: a tool and empty project, a page of rules, a brief, ship small, add a second agent later.
yours.para: The example is a shop owner. The book is part of the GEN ZX FOUNDERS series.

feedback.line: Does the story work, where did you stop reading, could you follow the last chapter?
feedback.para: Send a quick reaction on LinkedIn, or a page-specific comment as a public issue on the book's repository.

limits.line: A draft, rebuilt at every release; this describes the copy built 01:34 UTC on 3 November.
limits.para: The scenes are dramatised from the record; Leanpub is planned with no date set.

sources.line: The RC2 PDF, the RC2 page and the book's repository.
